title: Binary orbit and disks properties of the RW Aur system using ALMA observations
question: Nature (bound or unbound) of the RW Aur binary interaction and its impact on the dust and gas of the two disks, from multi-epoch 1.3 mm ALMA data

data.arrays: ACA 7m (SB2) plus 12m array up to configuration C-10 (LB1)
data.angular_resolution: LB1 continuum 18x30 mas (3 au in abstract); SB 12CO 267x414 mas; LB 12CO 69x98 mas

what.value: Historical astrometric separations of RW Aur A and B, epochs 1944 to 2013 (two outliers excluded)

evidence.loc: Results: RW Aur B orbit, with ALMA astrometry
evidence.quote: We combined our ALMA astrometry with the historical separation between RW Aur A and B as compiled by (cite: csepany2017), covering epochs from 1944 to 2013.

what.value: Dust mass absorption coefficient kappa_nu = 2.3 (nu/230 GHz)^0.4 cm2 g-1

evidence.quote: $\kappa_\nu=2.3(\nu/230\,\text{GHz})^{0.4}\,\text{cm}^{2}\text{g}^{-1}$ is the frequency-dependent mass absorption coefficient (cite: andrews2013)

what.value: Reference dust temperature of 20 K for the dust mass

evidence.quote: a known temperature, that is commonly set to 20 K for standard reference (cite: ansdell2016; cieza2019)

what.value: ALMA flux calibration uncertainty up to 10%

evidence.quote: it is known that the ALMA flux calibration uncertainties can reach up to 10%, and even higher in particular cases (cite: Andrews2018)

what.value: Stellar luminosities of RW Aur A and B (0.88 and 0.53 Lsun)

evidence.quote: The luminosities of stars A and B are 0.88$\,L_\odot$ and 0.53$\,L_\odot$, respectively (cite: Herczeg2014)

recipe.goal: Build and self-calibrate a pseudo-continuum for each project
recipe.method: Flag line channels, combine remaining channels with the continuum spws, average, and self-calibrate each project independently
key_parameters: Line channels within +/-25 km/s of VLSR (about 6 km/s) flagged
Averaged to 125 MHz channels and 6 s bins
Briggs robust 0.5 (LB1: 1.0) for self-cal images; observations not aligned to a common phase center before self-cal
assumptions: Each project treated as a single epoch

recipe.goal: Apply self-cal to line data, subtract continuum, image gas and make moment maps
recipe.method: Apply continuum self-cal tables to the original data, uvcontsub, tclean per line, combine epochs, then bettermoments for peak intensity, velocity, moment 0 and 1
key_parameters: tclean gain 0.05, cyclefactor 1.5, clean to 4 sigma, JvM correction
Channel width 1.3 km/s for LB 12CO, 0.5 km/s for SB 12CO
Moment images clipped at 0 sigma with no mask; extra LB 12CO image clipped at 1.3 mJy/beam km/s
assumptions: Spatial movement negligible across epochs at gas resolution, so epochs can be combined

recipe.goal: Fit parametric visibility models to the continuum of both disks
recipe.method: Joint multi-epoch fit with an axisymmetric brightness model per disk (A: point source + Gaussian + tapered power law; B: two Gaussian rings), visibilities of the two sources summed
key_parameters: Visibilities averaged to one channel per spw and 24 s; epochs not combined
All five epochs fit simultaneously with common intensity model but separate disk centers per epoch
Free per-epoch flux scale i_obs, SB4 fixed to 1
Model pixel size 4 mas (2 mas test gave consistent results)
assumptions: Each disk brightness distribution constant over the two years; only relative positions change

recipe.goal: Derive fluxes, brightness temperatures and dust masses
recipe.method: Integrate model images for flux; azimuthally averaged brightness temperature; dust mass from the Hildebrand formula
key_parameters: Dust temperature 20 K (also mean Tb of 27 K for RW Aur A within R90%)
assumptions: Optically thin dust at known temperature; fails for RW Aur A so only a lower limit
kappa_nu = 2.3 (nu/230 GHz)^0.4 cm2 g-1; distance 154 pc

recipe.goal: Test for a misaligned inner disk of RW Aur A
recipe.method: Repeat the visibility MCMC letting the central Gaussian have its own inclination and position angle
key_parameters: Same procedure as the main visibility fit

recipe.goal: Measure stellar masses from Keplerian rotation of the 12CO disks
recipe.method: Fit a flat Keplerian disk to the velocity maps with eddy
key_parameters: Elliptical emission masks of 0.4 and 0.28 arcsec for A and B; velocity pixels 4 mas, not downsampled
Center, inclination and PA fixed from the continuum outer-disk fit; free: stellar mass and systemic velocity
assumptions: Upper and lower emission surfaces cannot be distinguished, so a flat disk is assumed

recipe.goal: Measure gas disk radii and gas-to-dust size ratio
recipe.method: Integrate 12CO flux in elliptical apertures and find radii enclosing 68% and 90%; compare with continuum R90%
key_parameters: Aperture radii 0.6 arcsec (A) and 0.45 arcsec (B)
assumptions: Radii are measured from a beam-convolved profile, so the ratio is an upper limit

recipe.goal: Fit the orbit of RW Aur B around RW Aur A
recipe.method: MCMC over eight orbital parameters using ALMA disk-center astrometry, historical astrometry and one ALMA radial velocity; orbits computed with rebound for elliptical and hyperbolic regimes
key_parameters: Eight free parameters; 24 times as many walkers as free parameters
Uniform prior on positive eccentricity, excluding |1-ecc|<1e-4; periastron distance fitted instead of semi-major axis
Over 1e7 steps per walker; then one of every 80 steps recorded and last 1e5 recorded positions used
Radial velocity -0.954 km/s of B relative to A with 1 sigma set to 100 m/s
Two historical outliers (1991 and 1944 measurements) excluded
assumptions: Disk centers coincide with the stars; disks axisymmetric with zero eccentricity
Stars treated as point masses carrying the whole system mass

recipe.method: Akaike information criterion on the best 99.85 percentile of elliptical and hyperbolic models
key_parameters: Best 99.85 percentile of each family compared
assumptions: Only the astrometric likelihood is used; 12CO morphology not used as a prior

recipe.method: Compare disk inclination and PA (orientation set by the jet) with orbital inclination and node from the MCMC
assumptions: Disk is close to perpendicular to the jet

score_reason: Public ALMA projects and Zenodo self-calibrated products plus full model equations and numeric tables, but key MCMC and imaging settings, priors for the orbit fit, and historical astrometry values are missing and no code is released.
rediscovery_reason: Data are stated available (ALMA projects and Zenodo products), the visibility-fit and orbit-fit recipes are largely described, and results are numeric tables (disk sizes, fluxes, orbital elements).
